A ferry boat has sunk near Zamboanga City, with at least 18 dead.

The unfortunate tragedy has occurred merely 25 km from the prediction line for major accidents during Jan 16 to 28. In fact, I had especially pinpointed this very area as the most vulnerable. (See screenshot in 2nd picture of my website; the prediction had been published on Jan 15 itself.)

In addition, I have repeatedly warned that Jan 26 to 29 period is likely to bring major accidents as well as strong earthquakes in different parts of the world, especially in those areas which I have marked out as particularly vulnerable. I have also said that accidents in air and water are highly probable during this period.

There were more than 300 passengers on the ferry boat. I hope everyone else is rescued safe and sound.

Stay alert and safe!

data.raw_text:
COMPLAINT FILED VS MARIKINA POLICE OFFICER IN VIRAL VIDEO

Pasig City fire volunteer Earl Joseph Lantin officially filed a complaint against PSSg Michelle Ram De La Paz with the National Police Commission’s (NAPOLCOM) Inspection, Monitoring, and Investigation Service (IMIS) on Monday, Jan. 26, following a viral video showing the officer berating him in Marikina City.

NAPOLCOM Chief Commissioner Ralph Calinisan said the officer has been relieved from duty, but the investigation will continue. “Respect for civilians and fellow public servants is non-negotiable and central to police professionalism,” he emphasized.

The Marikina City police publicly announced on the evening of Jan. 23 that the officer from the viral video had been relieved even after settling with the vehicle’s owner. The Land Transportation Office had earlier issued a show-cause order against the officer, the fire truck’s owner, and its driver.

Courtesy: NAPOLCOM/Facebook

(via @war_noir)
